name: Tertullus
overview: Tertullus was a male attorney known for bringing formal charges against the Apostle Paul as recorded in Acts 24:2. Beyond his role as a legal advocate in this specific instance, Scripture does not provide additional personal details or tribal affiliations. His primary biblical significance lies in his function within this legal proceeding.
namesAndTitles: The name Tertullus appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Acts 24:2. No special meaning or divine origin is attributed to his name in the biblical record, indicating it is simply a proper name without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or connections for Tertullus beyond his role as an attorney bringing charges against Paul. There is no mention of relatives or associates in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Tertullus plays a notable role in the New Testament as the legal representative who formally accused Paul before Roman authorities. His involvement highlights the opposition Paul faced from Jewish leaders and the legal challenges encountered in spreading the gospel. Through Tertullus's accusations, the narrative demonstrates the tension between the early Christian message and established religious and civil powers.
